Below are several compact Altair examples you can run in Python (Jupyter, Colab, or a script that displays Vega charts) using a local seattle-weather.csv file. Adjust file path as needed. The CSV is expected to have at least: date, precipitation, temp_max, temp_min, wind, and weather.

Common setup:
```python
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

# read CSV (adjust path)
df = pd.read_csv("seattle-weather.csv", parse_dates=["date"])
```

1) Simple time series: daily precipitation
```python
chart = alt.Chart(df).mark_line(point=False).encode(
    x=alt.X("date:T", title="Date"),
    y=alt.Y("precipitation:Q", title="Precipitation (in)"),
    tooltip=["date:T", "precipitation:Q"]
).properties(
    title="Seattle Daily Precipitation",
    width=700, height=300
)
chart
```

2) Layered min/max temperature area + max line
```python
base = alt.Chart(df).encode(x=alt.X("date:T", title="Date"))

area = base.mark_area(opacity=0.2).encode(
    y=alt.Y("temp_min:Q", title="Temperature (°F)"),
    y2="temp_max:Q"
)

line = base.mark_line(color="firebrick").encode(
    y="temp_max:Q"
)

(area + line).properties(title="Daily Min/Max Temperature", width=700, height=300)
```

3) Weather category counts (bar chart)
```python
count_chart = alt.Chart(df).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("count():Q", title="Days"),
    y=alt.Y("weather:N", sort="-x", title="Weather"),
    color=alt.Color("weather:N", legend=None),
    tooltip=["weather:N", "count():Q"]
).properties(title="Days by Weather Type", width=600, height=300)
count_chart
```

4) Scatter: precipitation vs. max temp, colored by weather, sized by wind
```python
scatter = alt.Chart(df).mark_circle().encode(
    x=alt.X("precipitation:Q", title="Precipitation (in)"),
    y=alt.Y("temp_max:Q", title="Max Temp (°F)"),
    color=alt.Color("weather:N", title="Weather"),
    size=alt.Size("wind:Q", title="Wind Speed"),
    tooltip=["date:T", "precipitation:Q", "temp_max:Q", "wind:Q", "weather:N"]
).properties(title="Precipitation vs Max Temperature", width=700, height=400)
scatter
```

5) Faceted monthly overview (average precipitation per month by year)
```python
df["year"] = df["date"].dt.year
df["month"] = df["date"].dt.month

monthly = df.groupby(["year", "month"], as_index=False).agg(
    precipitation=("precipitation", "mean")
)

facet = alt.Chart(monthly).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("month:O", title="Month"),
    y=alt.Y("precipitation:Q", title="Avg Precipitation"),
    color=alt.Color("month:O", legend=None)
).properties(width=120, height=120).facet(
    column=alt.Column("year:O", title=None)
)
facet
```

Notes:
- If running in a non-Jupyter environment, call chart.show() or save charts to HTML with chart.save("chart.html").
- If you prefer to use the vega_datasets packaged copy of this CSV (if installed), you can load it with:
  from vega_datasets import data
  df = data.seattle_weather()
- Customize marks, encodings, and interactivity (selection) as desired.
